Description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa continues the previous sermon's conclusion that God is doing everything and turns to the rearranging of priorities, diagramming the human being as a body that lasts perhaps a hundred years and a soul that lasts forever. He argues that people devote schooling, careers and money to the vanishing body while starving the real person, citing Rock Hudson and Liberace as cases of fame and wealth that left the soul undeveloped, and reads Sura 18:45-47 on this world as vegetation turning to hay and on money and children as its adornments. The second sermon contrasts a believer's morning with a neighbor's and stresses commemorating God throughout the day, then presents a passage he asks the congregation to identify, which argues that no letter of a prayer text may be added or omitted because any change destroys an inherent numerical harmony. He applies that argument to the addition of "Amen" to Al-Fatehah and to the Quranic warning addressed to those who are heedless of their prayers.
